A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Stereo4D and DynaDUSt3R work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplements support comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original training and evaluation results for motion and structure prediction on Stereo4D, ADT, and Bonn, including Tables 1–2 and qualitative experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds loss-component and motion-head ablations, frame-gap sensitivity results, and camera-motion analyses.

M1.justification: The data-processing pipeline, track-optimization objective, DynaDUSt3R architecture, and prediction losses remain unchanged. The newly evaluated single-head variant is an experimental ablation.

E1.justification: Both versions use Stereo4D and PointOdyssey for training and Stereo4D, ADT, and Bonn for evaluation. Added analyses reuse existing Stereo4D coverage; the frame-gap analysis stays within the existing 0–30-frame evaluation range.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 15 newly evaluates BiDAStereo against the track-optimization pipeline; v1 only cited that work. The comparator sets in the main motion and depth benchmarks remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds a frame-gap analysis over 1,000 Stereo4D pairs and controlled loss/head comparisons. Appendix weight decay changes from 0.95 to 0.05, although Section 4 still states 0.95. This is a reported setting revision with an unresolved inconsistency; the PDFs do not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: V1 provides before/after track-optimization examples. V2 adds controlled tests of the static and dynamic losses, separate versus shared prediction heads, and sensitivity to frame spacing in Section 8. These substantially expand validation of choices in both the reconstruction pipeline and predictor.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new frame-gap curve has no error bars; its discussion of uncertainty does not introduce statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New results show static-track drift without the static loss, distorted trajectories without the dynamic loss, and worse single-head accuracy: EPE 0.1401 versus 0.1110, with threshold accuracies 59.19/69.73 versus 65.07/75.18. Frame-gap errors and additional camera distributions further expand the findings. Tables 1–2 retain all original values.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, motion definitions, optimization objectives, and geometric formulas are retained. V2 introduces no new theoretical result, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: scalable pseudo-metric 4D reconstruction from internet stereo videos and using that data to learn geometry and motion with DynaDUSt3R.

C2.justification: V2 tentatively attributes the single-head accuracy drop to reduced decoder capacity and larger-gap errors to increased motion magnitude and uncertainty. It also explains the distinct effects of the two track losses. Existing limitations and future directions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 Section 7 adds the YouTube collection tag, source and derived-data licensing information, and a direct link to the stated release of geometry, motion data, and video links. The appendix also revises weight decay, creating the conflict with Section 4 noted under E3.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Pixel-perfect Structure-from-Motion and VGGSfM to its discussion of point-track representations. Broader research positioning remains stable; publication updates and duplicate-reference cleanup do not introduce additional distinct prior works.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized language and terminology edits, adds appendix cross-references, and inserts an Ablations section with subsequent appendix renumbering. The main narrative organization and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 12, 14, and 15 for camera statistics, frame-gap sensitivity, and track ablations. Table 1 moves from page 6 to page 7, and existing appendix figures are repositioned and renumbered. The overall layout and existing visual content are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The added ablations strengthen support for the loss and motion-head choices, while the sensitivity analysis and data-access information improve evaluation and reuse documentation. These are useful, bounded gains. The new contradiction between appendix weight decay 0.05 and Section 4's 0.95 introduces reproducibility ambiguity that partially offsets them.
